- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–20%.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 3–5 day highs) — cap forecast overshoot at 20% above recent peak.
- Model underestimates long-term mean reversion; if 10+ days of price stability, forecast should trend toward historical mean (avg of last 10–15 days).
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (e.g., >5σ from mean) unless sentiment strongly supports them.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model often fails to catch momentum — adjust forecast upward by 5–15% if sentiment turns bullish.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–2 days — if sentiment turns positive, forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true price movement.
